newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian officials deny gold swap talks with UBS.
newsitem.headline: Russian officials deny gold swap talks with UBS.

text.p: Russian financial officials on Friday denied precious metal market rumours that Russia was in talks with Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) to swap gold for platinum and palladium.
A senior Central Bank representative said no talks to this effect had taken place with UBS.
Asked about the rumours, Sergei Kyshtymov, head of the precious metals operations section of the Central Bank, said "There have been no such talks."
Platinum prices leaped earlier this week on rumours Russia was discussing a swap of stockpiled platinum and palladium for 30 tonnes of gold the Swiss bank was holding as collateral.
"There was an assumption that the platinum market had fallen into concentrated hands," a precious metal markets source said.
"When dealers heard these rumours a lot of people came piling in on the basis that the palladium price had gone roaring up and now it was platinum's turn," he said.

Russia is the world's largest supplier of palladium and Japan the world's largest consumer. Protracted delays to 1997 contract negotiations between the two countries have triggered a sharp rise in world palladium prices this year.
Administrative snags in Russia have been cited as the reason behind the delay in negotiations and the drying up of exports.
Kyshtymov added that the Central Bank was in contact with several European banks and the two sides could cooperate on a general level in the future.
"We are working with a lot of these banks," he said in a telephone interview.
However of future discussions, he added,"Such a plan is not on my agenda, but I can't be in charge of everything," he said.

Kyshtymov also played down talk among traders in Tokyo that Russian Central Bank officials may go to Japan next week to discuss deals whereby Russia makes precious metals available to Japanese commercial banks as collateral for loans.
"There will not be such a delegation (to Japan next week), because the palladium supply delays are resolved by the government and not the Central Bank," he said.
Vladimir Rybkin, head of the Finance Ministry's precious senior precious metals department also played down market talk of possible swaps with overseas banks.
"No, there have been no such talks," he said. "But it would be interesting to find out where the rumour originated," he added.
Rybkin also said he was unaware of any Central Bank mission going to Japan soon.
"I still have no information on whether a delegation plans to go to Japan next week," he said.

Traders have speculated that possible precious metal swaps or deliveries as collateral to foreign banks could be part of a major overhaul of the way Russia's often archaic and always secretive precious metals market is run.
The government still has a tight grip over production and exports of gold, platinum, palladium and diamonds.
But on Friday First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said Russia needs radical changes to its gold market and that concrete proposals for liberalising it would be made within the next ten days.

Kyshtymov said the Central Bank was still waiting for the Russian government to sign a decree on precious metals exports which would allow long-delayed platinum group metal supplies to Japan to begin.
"We are still waiting for the signing of the government decree. We don't know when the deal will be signed."

Precious metals market sources in London speculated that the rumours about Russia reflected the apparent shifting of power within the country's administration on precious metals exporting responsibility.
"The central bank seems to be taking over (from Almaz the former export agency)," one source usually close to Russian business said.

"The have to raise money without just printing it and the Central Bank appears to have been charged with that task. All they can do is sell off the family silver," he added. --Mike Collett-White, Moscow Newsroom +7095 941 8520
